title: Why Does Soap Remove Grease?
topic: Why does soap remove grease and oil when plain water cannot?
claims: Water molecules are polar and do not mix with non-polar grease due to hydrophobic interactions.
Soap molecules possess a polar hydrophilic head and a non-polar hydrophobic tail.
Soap forms micelles around grease, allowing it to be rinsed away by water.
Hot water increases molecular kinetic energy, speeding up the dissolving and melting of fats.

title: How Vaccines Train Your Immune System
topic: How do vaccines actually train your immune system to fight real viruses?
claims: Vaccines deliver a harmless piece or blueprint of the pathogen to stimulate an immune response.
White blood cells detect foreign antigens and produce specific antibodies.
Memory cells store the genetic information required to produce those specific antibodies upon re-exposure.
Booster shots enhance the immune response by reinforcing memory cell populations.

sources.cite: Abayasingam et al. (2021), Cell Reports Medicine. doi:10.1016/j.xcrm.2021.100228
sources.claim: Memory cells store the genetic information required to produce those specific antibodies upon re-exposure.

title: Why Does Baking Soda Fizz With Vinegar
topic: Why does baking soda fizz when mixed with vinegar?
claims: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (a base).
Vinegar contains acetic acid.
The reaction creates sodium acetate, water, and carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide gas causes the fizzing.
Unreacted baking soda is basic and bitter.

title: Why Do Objects Fall At The Same Rate? 😲
topic: Why do heavy and light objects fall at the same speed? The physics of gravity
claims: Gravity accelerates all objects at the same rate in a vacuum regardless of mass (Equivalence Principle).
F = ma, so a = F/m. Since F is proportional to mass (F = GmM/r^2), the 'm' in the numerator and denominator cancel out.
Inertia is the resistance to acceleration, which is exactly why heavier objects are harder to move but also experience more gravitational force.

title: How Salt Melts Ice: Chemistry Explained
topic: Why does salt melt ice on frozen roads? The chemistry of freezing point depression
claims: Water molecules on ice constantly shift between solid and liquid phases.
Sodium and chloride ions dissolve into the surface liquid layer.
Dissolved ions physically interfere with water molecules rejoining the crystal lattice.
Freezing point depression lowers the temperature at which ice can remain solid.
Eutectic point of NaCl-water is approximately -21.1 degrees Celsius.

title: How Colour Vision Works: The Biology of Cone Cells Explained
topic: How colour vision works: The biology of cone cells explained
claims: Human trichromatic color vision relies on three cone cell types (S, M, L) responding to overlapping spectral sensitivity curves.
A red object reflects long wavelengths primarily, stimulating L-cones most heavily, but color perception is determined by the brain processing the ratio of activation across all three cone types.
Protanopia is the absence or malfunction of long-wavelength (L) cone photopigments, causing red colors to appear dark or dull.

title: When Does A Lens Flip The Image?
topic: Why does a lens flip the image I see?
claims: Lenses converge light rays to a focal point.
Light from the top of an object passes through the lens and is redirected to the bottom of the image plane, causing inversion.
The virtual image produced within the focal length is upright and magnified.
Cameras use lens convergence to focus real, inverted images onto sensors.

title: Why Does a Siren Change Pitch? The Doppler Effect
topic: Why does a siren change pitch as it passes? The Doppler effect explained
claims: Sound wave crests bunch up ahead of a moving sound source and spread apart behind it.
Perceived pitch is directly proportional to the frequency of sound waves hitting the ear.
The speed of sound in air is determined by properties of the air (temperature, density) and is independent of source velocity.

sources.cite: Usagawa et al. (1987), Journal of the Acoustical Society of Japan (E). doi:10.1250/ast.8.23
sources.claim: Sound wave crests bunch up ahead of a moving sound source and spread apart behind it.

sources.cite: Rabenstein et al. (2017), Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing. doi:10.1155/2017/9524943
sources.claim: The speed of sound in air is determined by properties of the air (temperature, density) and is independent of source velocity.

title: Why Don't Planets Fall Into The Sun?
topic: Why don't planets fall into the Sun? Celestial orbits explained
claims: Planets stay in orbit because their tangential velocity is sufficient to counteract the gravitational pull of the Sun.
If tangential velocity is removed, an object will fall directly toward the center of gravity.
Orbits are effectively a continuous state of falling while moving fast enough to miss the central body.

sources.cite: Tsang (2025), Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research). doi:10.5281/zenodo.20150543
sources.claim: Orbits are effectively a continuous state of falling while moving fast enough to miss the central body.

claims: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) is a base.
Vinegar (dilute acetic acid) is an acid.
The reaction produces water, sodium acetate, and carbon dioxide gas.
Gas production creates the physical foaming effect.

Antibodies are specific to the antigen shape they were developed for.
mRNA vaccines use cellular machinery to produce harmless spike proteins.

title: Why Does An LED Need A Resistor?
topic: Why do I actually need a resistor for an LED?
claims: LEDs are current-controlled devices and lack internal current-limiting mechanisms.
Resistors in series with LEDs follow Ohm's Law (V=IR) to limit current.
Excess current causes thermal damage to the semiconductor junction in an LED.
Increasing resistance in a series circuit decreases the total current.
